items.source_excerpt: The role of the UK Emissions Trading Scheme in UK decarbonisation and how the UK ETS Authority is developing the scheme. The UK Emissions Trading Scheme ( UK ETS ) currently covers the heavy industry, power and aviation sectors – approximately 25% of UK territorial emissions. The scheme incentivises investment in decarbonisation in line with climate targets across the UK, by setting a cap on emissions from these sectors and creating a carbon price. The UK ETS Authority (consisting of the UK, Scottish, and Welsh Governments, and the Northern Ireland Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs) is working to expand and develop the scheme to incentivise additional sectors of the economy. This sets out: the policy aims of the UK ETS how it works the work the UK ETS Authority is doing to develop it We will update the content as further policy updates are published. items.source_excerpt: Find out how sector-level CBAM rates are calculated under the CBAM rate methodology using illustrative rates and worked example. The UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism ( CBAM ) is designed to address the risk of carbon leakage as the UK decarbonises its economy. It does this by applying a carbon price to imported goods in covered sectors that reflects the carbon price faced by comparable domestic production. Unlike most taxes, CBAM does not have a single headline rate set out in primary legislation. Instead, the rate is determined using a methodology that combines recent carbon pricing data, sector-level emissions information and the extent to which domestic producers continue to receive free allowances under the UK Emissions Trading Scheme. This methodology is set out in law, via the Finance Act 2026. The purpose of this note is to explain how sector-level CBAM rates are calculated under the CBAM rate methodology. It is intended as a transparency tool to help businesses understand…
